prompt.context: Our client is a national portable sanitation provider in the U.S. Their revenue primarily comes from renting out port-a-potties to construction sites, events, etc. They also have a smaller business in temporary fencing (such as for construction sites) and mobile dumpsters. Revenue has been decreasing in recent years.
prompt.question: The client would like you to provide a strategy to increase revenue over the next few years.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any objectives besides increasing revenue?
clarifying_info.a: No other objectives besides to increase revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Is the focus U.S. only or global?
What is the client's role in the supply chain?
clarifying_info.a: The client is the 'middle man' – purchases port-a-potties from manufacturer and deploys to sites. Will handle maintenance and cleanup afterwards.

clarifying_info.q: How does the client currently get business?
clarifying_info.a: Has an online presence but primarily gets business via phone/in-person relationships.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current rental pricing?
clarifying_info.a: Rental income of $2,000 per toilet per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue breakdown by product?
clarifying_info.a: Port-a-potties make up 90% of the business, which is currently $200mm/year.
Yes, customers are very sensitive to price; it is 2nd in priority only to service/quality.

exhibits.title: Results of Price Increase Test
exhibits.shows: A table comparing original vs. test results for a price increase experiment at one branch, showing price, volume, variable cost per toilet, and fixed cost.

framework: Organic Revenue Increase: Pricing (demand elasticity, competitor rates) and Volume (customer demand, competitor market share, geographical demand, other channels)
Mix shift: grow higher-margin products (port-a-potties vs. temporary fencing vs. mobile dumpsters vs. new offerings)
Inorganic Revenue Increase: acquire market share, joint ventures with industry stakeholders, vertical integration

questions.prompt: Should the client consider raising prices to increase revenue? Use Exhibit 1 to support your answer.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate revenue under both scenarios, note that a 5% price increase drove a 20% volume decline, and conclude that demand is highly elastic so raising prices would decrease revenue. Strong candidates also calculate profit impact.

math.setup: Compare revenue and profit at original price vs. test (raised) price using Exhibit 1 data.
math.answer: A 5% price increase caused a 20% volume drop, reducing revenue by ~$320K and profit by ~$80K. Demand is highly elastic; the client should NOT raise prices.

questions.prompt: What else can the client do to grow revenue beyond pricing?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore volume growth levers, geographic expansion, and inorganic options. Strong answers distinguish between organic and inorganic growth and prioritize based on market opportunity data (e.g., low market share + high market opportunity in Southwest).

brainstorming.prompt: How can the client grow revenue?

categories.name: Organic – Pricing
ideas: Assess competitor pricing to find headroom if elasticity allows
Introduce tiered pricing or premium service tiers
Bundle products (sanitation + fencing + dumpsters) for larger contracts

categories.name: Organic – Volume
ideas: Improve efficacy of marketing spend (digital channels, SEO)
Expand geographic footprint, especially in high-opportunity/low-share regions like the Southwest
Target underpenetrated customer segments (e.g., events, disaster relief)
Strengthen in-person and phone sales relationships

categories.name: Mix
ideas: Grow temporary fencing and mobile dumpster segments

categories.name: Inorganic
ideas: Acquire a competitor in the Southwest to gain immediate market share
Joint venture with industry stakeholders (construction firms, event organizers)
Vertical integration: acquire a port-a-potty manufacturer to reduce COGS
Invest in R&D for innovative product with better quality
Start offering maintenance service as a new revenue stream

recommendation: Recommend growing revenue by increasing market share in the Southwest region, which has low current market capture but high nominal market opportunity.
risks: Market entry execution risk and cost overruns
Competitor response (price war or aggressive expansion)
Management distraction from core business during expansion
next_steps: Start a work stream to determine cost breakdown for Southwest expansion
Build operational capacity (equipment, staff, logistics) to enter the market
